summary: Comprehensive deep dive into Dynadot backorder mechanics. Key finding: Dynadot ONLY accepts backorders for domains currently in pendingDelete status. The 'could not find backorder' error from Sprint 24/25 confirms our domains are NOT yet in Dynadot's pendingDelete inventory. Dynadot has ~15 ICANN accreditations vs DropCatch's ~1,200 — catch rate is roughly 1% vs DropCatch per domain. For Tier S targets, Dynadot alone is insufficient.

backorder_timing.earliest_acceptance: Domain MUST be in pendingDelete status at the registry level. Dynadot cannot accept backorders for domains in grace period, auto-renew period, redemption period, clientHold, or clientRenewProhibited. The domain must appear in Dynadot's pendingDelete inventory list before a backorder can be placed.
backorder_timing.optimal_timing: Place backorder IMMEDIATELY when pendingDelete status is detected via RDAP/WHOIS. The pendingDelete window is only 5 days. Earlier is better — Dynadot gives chronological priority to first backorder requester if multiple people backorder the same domain.
backorder_timing.too_late: Once the domain drops (day 5 of pendingDelete), it is released to the public and becomes a race between registrar accreditations. Backorder must be placed BEFORE the drop, during the 5-day pendingDelete window.
backorder_timing.key_constraint: Our drop_monitor.py already auto-triggers backorder on pendingDelete detection (line 510: if transition.current_status in ('pendingDelete', 'available')). The 6-hour cron interval may miss the window — consider increasing frequency to every 1-2 hours for domains within 7 days of estimated pendingDelete.
backorder_timing.sprint25_evidence: All 19 backorder attempts on 2026-05-15 returned 'could not find backorder fot this domain' — confirming none are in pendingDelete yet. guerrameats.com is in clientHold, sunnyray.org and globalgeopark.org are in autoRenewPeriod.

estimated_dynadot_catch_rate.uncontested_domain: 50-70% (if Dynadot is the only service attempting to catch)

catch_rate.vs_dropcatch: DropCatch catches 50%+ of all drop-caught .com domains due to massive accreditation advantage. DropCatch full-price ($59) achieves 60-80% for moderately competitive domains. Dynadot is described as 'competing with Pheenix for the bottom of the food chain' in drop-catching (NamePros community).
catch_rate.for_org_tld: .org domains have significantly less drop-catch competition than .com. Fewer professional domainers target .org. Dynadot's relative chance improves materially for .org — estimated 15-30% for niche .org domains like sunnyray.org and globalgeopark.org.
catch_rate.dropcatch_decline_2024: DropCatch's per-registrar catch rate declined 57% from Dec 2023 to Dec 2024 (58 domains/registrar/month to 25). ICANN fee overhead rose from ~$8 to ~$18 per domain caught. May reduce accreditations in future.
catch_rate.source_notes: Accreditation numbers from NamePros threads and DomainNameWire (April 2025). Exact catch rates are proprietary — estimates based on community reports.

multi_platform_strategy.for_tier_s_domains: Dynadot alone is INSUFFICIENT. For guerrameats.com (ETV $11,376), must use DropCatch ($59) as primary catcher + Dynadot ($10.99) as cheap backup. Consider SnapNames ($79) as third layer.
multi_platform_strategy.how_multi_platform_works: Only ONE platform catches any given domain (the one whose registrar accreditation wins the registry race). You only pay the winning platform. Other platforms charge $0. No risk of double-payment.

tier_s_critical_domains.total_cost_if_caught: Pay only winning platform ($10.99-$79 depending on who catches)
tier_s_critical_domains.combined_catch_probability: 70-90% for niche domains, 40-60% for moderate competition

multi_platform_strategy.cancellation: Yes — Dynadot backorders can be cancelled via delete_backorder_request API or web UI at any time before the domain drops. If DropCatch catches a domain, you can cancel the Dynadot backorder (though it would auto-fail anyway since another registrar won).
multi_platform_strategy.auction_risk: If multiple USERS place backorders on the SAME platform for the same domain, it goes to auction. DropCatch: public 3-day auction. SnapNames/Dynadot: private auction among backorder holders only.

phase_1_grace.name: Auto-Renew Grace Period
phase_1_grace.description: Domain expired but registrar auto-renewed. Owner can pay renewal to keep it. DNS may still work.

phase_2_auction.name: Registrar Internal Auction (if applicable)
phase_2_auction.description: Some registrars (GoDaddy, Tucows, Squarespace, Name.com) send expired domains to GoDaddy Auctions before deletion. If sold here, domain NEVER reaches pendingDelete.

phase_3_closeout.name: GoDaddy Closeout (reverse auction)
phase_3_closeout.description: If no bids in auction, domain enters declining-price closeout ($30 -> $15 -> $5). First-come, first-served.

phase_4_redemption.name: Redemption Grace Period
phase_4_redemption.description: Domain deleted from registrar. Registry holds it. Original owner can restore with $80-$150+ fee. NO backorders possible during this phase.

phase_5_pending_delete.name: pendingDelete
phase_5_pending_delete.description: IRREVERSIBLE. Domain scheduled for deletion. Cannot be recovered by anyone. THIS is when Dynadot accepts backorders. RDAP status shows 'pending delete' or 'pendingDelete'.

phase_6_drop.name: Domain Drop
phase_6_drop.description: Domain released to registry pool. Drop-catch services race to register. Whoever's registrar accreditation sends the fastest EPP create command wins.
